QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_33

question.text: Under SAS-400, sanitary-pad distribution is listed as a SAS-400 intervention. A common indicator is 'School attendance days gained by adolescent girls'. The MOST robust DATA SOURCE is:

answer.text: School attendance register + pad-distribution tally + adolescent-girl self-report + nurse/teacher corroboration

explanation.text: The Logic: Multi-source: school attendance (administrative), distribution register (SE), girl self-report (primary), teacher corroboration (secondary primary). This matches the Sakhi case-study's triangulation approach. The Trap: Options A, C, D are single-source or irrelevant sources. Cross-Exam Context: Same multi-source evidence principle as SAS-200 healthcare cases and III-A / III-C Compliance. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Sanitary-pad programmes often overstate 'days gained' — anchor the outcome to actual school-register attendance not self-report estimates.
